Key Cross-Corpus Structural Insights:
  • APA Core Journals Benchmark (2023–2025, N = 9,663): Across 80 society flagship journals in 2023, 2024, and 2025 (99.6% full-text coverage), APA Core Journals comprise 7,914 empirical studies (6,342 Pure Quantitative, 675 Mixed Methods, 627 Qualitative, and 270 Meta-Analyses) alongside 1,712 theoretical reviews, commentaries, and methodological papers.
  • International OA Mega-Journals vs. Society Flagships: PLOS ONE Psychology (66.5% Pure Quant, 83.6% Empirical), Frontiers in Psychology (66.3% Pure Quant, 79.8% Empirical), and BMC Psychology (78.6% Pure Quant, 90.5% Empirical) publish predominantly empirical research (plus 2,105 study protocols and reviews in PLOS ONE), whereas APA Core Journals (2023–2025) dedicate 17.7% of their pages to theoretical reviews, methodological papers, and commentaries (and 2.8% to Meta-Analyses).
  • Thai TCI Tier 1 & Chula Theses: Thai academic venues feature substantially higher proportions of Mixed Methods (18.2% in TCI 1 Core Psych; 13.6% in Chula M.A. and 30.2% in Chula Ph.D. dissertations) and Qualitative / CQR research, creating a strong denominator effect when comparing raw statistical prevalence.

SEM / CFA Estimators & Psychometric Reporting Highlights

Comparison of latent variable estimation algorithms and scale validation practices across international and Thai cohorts.

1. Latent Variable Estimators in APA vs. Frontiers/BMC
Among SEM/CFA papers in APA (2023–2025), 37.6% report standard Maximum Likelihood (ML), 17.2% use Robust Maximum Likelihood (MLR), and 8.8% use ordinal weighted least squares (WLSMV / DWLS), reflecting strong awareness of ordinal Likert non-normality.
2. McDonald's Omega (ω) vs. Cronbach's Alpha (α)
While Cronbach's α remains dominant across all corpora, McDonald's ω is reported in 3.8%–4.5% of APA quantitative studies in 2023–2025 (over 280 articles), whereas Thai TCI 1 and Chula theses emphasize Content Validity (IOC / CVI: 34.8% in Chula), Pilot Try-out (25.1%), and Back-Translation (13.2%).
3. CB-SEM vs. PLS-SEM Cultural Divide
APA Core Journals (0.3% PLS-SEM) and Chula Psychology Theses (0.1% PLS-SEM) rely almost exclusively on covariance-based SEM (CB-SEM: 15.3% in APA, 29.2% in Chula Grad). By contrast, Frontiers (3.4%), BMC (4.2%), and The Journal of Behavioral Science (TJBS) (22.8% in 2022–2026) show substantial adoption of variance-based PLS-SEM (SmartPLS).

Complete all-years longitudinal analysis across 5 journals (TJCP, TJBS, KJSS, AJHSS_BUU, CMU_JHUMANS) tracking the rise of CB-SEM, PLS-SEM, CFA, and software transitions.

Era (AD) Total Quant CB-SEM PLS-SEM CFA Any SEM (% Quant) Software Transition
1980-2005 395 34 1 0 0 1 (2.9% of Quant) AMOS: 0 | LISREL: 0 | SmartPLS: 0 | Mplus: 0
2006-2010 209 80 11 0 4 11 (13.8% of Quant) AMOS: 2 | LISREL: 6 | SmartPLS: 0 | Mplus: 0
2011-2015 337 159 20 0 6 20 (12.6% of Quant) AMOS: 1 | LISREL: 6 | SmartPLS: 0 | Mplus: 0
2016-2020 842 441 110 8 50 112 (25.4% of Quant) AMOS: 24 | LISREL: 22 | SmartPLS: 6 | Mplus: 8
2021-2026 1,476 808 247 58 186 256 (31.7% of Quant) AMOS: 50 | LISREL: 25 | SmartPLS: 29 | Mplus: 21
Generational Software Shift in Thailand: In 2006–2015, LISREL was the dominant SEM package in Thai journals. After 2016, AMOS (80 papers), SmartPLS (37 papers), and Mplus (29 papers) overtook LISREL.
